courses.title: Medical Terminology and the Health Professions
courses.description: Word roots, prefixes and suffixes, anatomical position and directional terms, and the roles of the health-care team in Nigeria.

topics.title: Building Medical Words: Roots, Prefixes and Suffixes
topics.summary: How medical terms are formed from Greek and Latin parts.

material.heading: Word parts
material.body: Most medical terms combine a root (the core meaning), an optional prefix (at the start) and a suffix (at the end), often joined by a combining vowel 'o'. Examples of roots: cardi (heart), hepat (liver), nephr/ren (kidney), gastr (stomach), oste (bone), neur (nerve), derm (skin), haem/hem (blood), pulmon/pneum (lung), enter (intestine), cyst (bladder), hyster/metr (uterus).

material.heading: Common prefixes and suffixes
material.body: Prefixes: hyper- (above normal), hypo- (below normal), tachy- (fast), brady- (slow), dys- (difficult/abnormal), a-/an- (without), poly- (many), peri- (around), endo- (within), hemi- (half). Suffixes: -itis (inflammation), -ectomy (surgical removal), -otomy (cutting into), -ostomy (making an opening), -algia (pain), -emia/-aemia (blood condition), -penia (deficiency), -megaly (enlargement), -plasty (surgical repair), -scopy (visual examination), -uria (urine).

questions.stem: The suffix '-ectomy' means:
questions.explanation: e.g. appendicectomy = removal of the appendix.

questions.stem: 'Hepatomegaly' means:
questions.explanation: hepat = liver; -megaly = enlargement.

questions.stem: A heart rate of 130 beats per minute in an adult is described as:
questions.explanation: tachy- means fast; tachycardia is > 100 bpm.

questions.stem: The root 'nephr' refers to the:
questions.explanation: Nephron, nephritis — nephr = kidney.

questions.stem: 'Thrombocytopenia' means:
questions.explanation: thrombocyte = platelet; -penia = deficiency.

questions.stem: 'Dysuria' means:
questions.explanation: dys- = difficult; -uria = urine.

questions.stem: Creating a surgical opening from the colon to the abdominal wall is a:
questions.explanation: -ostomy = making an opening (stoma).

questions.stem: The prefix 'hypo-' means:
questions.explanation: e.g. hypoglycaemia = low blood glucose.

topics.title: Anatomical Position, Planes and Directional Terms
topics.summary: The standard reference position, body planes, directions and body cavities.

material.heading: Position and planes
material.body: In the anatomical position the body stands erect, facing forward, feet together, arms by the sides with palms facing forward. The sagittal plane divides the body into right and left parts (the midsagittal/median plane into equal halves); the coronal (frontal) plane divides it into anterior and posterior parts; the transverse (axial/horizontal) plane divides it into superior and inferior parts — CT scans display transverse slices.
keyPoints: Palms face forward in anatomical position
Sagittal: left/right; coronal: front/back; transverse: top/bottom

material.heading: Directional terms and cavities
material.body: Anterior/ventral (front) vs posterior/dorsal (back); superior/cranial vs inferior/caudal; medial (towards the midline) vs lateral (away); proximal (closer to the trunk or origin of a limb) vs distal; superficial vs deep; ipsilateral (same side) vs contralateral (opposite side). The dorsal cavity contains the cranial and vertebral cavities; the ventral cavity contains the thoracic cavity (pleural and pericardial) and the abdominopelvic cavity, separated by the diaphragm. The abdomen is described in nine regions or four quadrants.
keyPoints: Proximal = nearer the trunk; distal = farther

questions.stem: In the anatomical position, the palms face:
questions.explanation: Palms face anteriorly in the anatomical position.

questions.stem: A plane dividing the body into anterior and posterior parts is the:
questions.explanation: The coronal (frontal) plane separates front from back.

questions.stem: The elbow is ___ to the wrist.
questions.explanation: The elbow is closer to the trunk than the wrist.

questions.stem: The thumb is on the ___ side of the hand (anatomical position).
questions.explanation: With palms forward, the thumb lies laterally.

questions.stem: Standard CT images are displayed in which plane?
questions.explanation: CT slices are usually axial (transverse).

questions.stem: A stroke in the right cerebral hemisphere causes weakness on the ___ side of the body.
questions.explanation: Motor pathways cross, so the weakness is on the opposite (left) side.

questions.stem: The structure separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities is the:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the musculotendinous partition between them.

questions.stem: The term 'superficial' means:
questions.explanation: Superficial = nearer the surface; deep = farther from it.

topics.title: Body Organisation and Systems
topics.summary: Levels of organisation, the four basic tissues and overview of organ systems.

material.heading: Levels of organisation
material.body: The body is organised from chemical → cellular → tissue → organ → organ system → organism. There are four basic tissue types: epithelial (covers surfaces and lines cavities), connective (supports and binds — bone, cartilage, blood, adipose tissue), muscular (skeletal, cardiac and smooth) and nervous tissue (neurons and neuroglia).
keyPoints: Four tissues: epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous

material.heading: Organ systems
material.body: Major systems: integumentary (skin), skeletal, muscular, nervous, endocrine, cardiovascular, lymphatic/immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, and reproductive. Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment, mostly by negative feedback (e.g. temperature regulation, blood glucose control by insulin and glucagon). Positive feedback amplifies a change and is rare (e.g. oxytocin in labour, blood clotting).

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the four basic tissue types?
questions.explanation: The four basic tissues are epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous.

questions.stem: Blood is classified as a type of:
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue.

questions.stem: The correct order of organisation is:
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems.

questions.stem: Most homeostatic mechanisms work by:
questions.explanation: Negative feedback reverses deviations from the set point.

questions.stem: An example of positive feedback is:
questions.explanation: Uterine contractions stimulate more oxytocin, amplifying labour.

questions.stem: The skin belongs to the ___ system.
questions.explanation: Skin, hair and nails form the integumentary system.

questions.stem: Which muscle type is found in the walls of blood vessels and the gut?
questions.explanation: Smooth (involuntary, non-striated) muscle lines hollow organs.

questions.stem: The hormone that lowers blood glucose is:
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and storage.

topics.title: The Health-Care Team and Professional Regulation in Nigeria
topics.summary: Roles of health professionals and the councils that regulate them.

material.heading: Members of the team
material.body: Care is delivered by an interprofessional team: doctors and dentists diagnose and treat; nurses and midwives provide continuous patient care; pharmacists dispense and advise on medicines; medical laboratory scientists perform diagnostic tests; radiographers produce medical images; physiotherapists restore movement and function; community health workers (CHEWs) deliver primary care; dietitians, health information managers and biomedical engineers also contribute. Effective teamwork depends on communication, mutual respect and clear roles.

material.heading: Regulatory councils
material.body: Each profession is regulated by a statutory council that registers practitioners and accredits training: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN); Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN); Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN); Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria (MLSCN); Radiographers Registration Board of Nigeria (RRBN); Medical Rehabilitation Therapists Board (physiotherapy); Community Health Practitioners Registration Board (CHPRBN). The National Universities Commission (NUC) accredits university programmes.
keyPoints: PCN: pharmacists; MLSCN: lab scientists; RRBN: radiographers

questions.stem: Which body registers medical doctors in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria registers doctors and dentists.

questions.stem: Pharmacists in Nigeria are regulated by the:
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria regulates pharmacy practice.

questions.stem: The Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria is abbreviated:
questions.explanation: MLSCN regulates medical laboratory scientists.

questions.stem: Radiographers are registered by the:
questions.explanation: The Radiographers Registration Board of Nigeria registers radiographers.

questions.stem: The body that accredits university degree programmes is the:
questions.explanation: The National Universities Commission accredits university programmes.

questions.stem: Nurses and midwives are regulated by the:
questions.explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria regulates them.

questions.stem: Restoring movement and function after injury is mainly the role of the:
questions.explanation: Physiotherapists specialise in movement rehabilitation.

questions.stem: Which factor most improves interprofessional teamwork?
questions.explanation: Communication and respect underpin safe team care.

topics.title: Abbreviations, Prescriptions and Vital Signs
topics.summary: Common clinical abbreviations, prescription terms and normal vital signs.

material.heading: Clinical abbreviations
material.body: Common prescription abbreviations (from Latin): od — once daily; bd — twice daily; tds — three times daily; qds — four times daily; nocte — at night; stat — immediately; prn — as needed; po — by mouth; IV — intravenous; IM — intramuscular; SC — subcutaneous; ac — before meals; pc — after meals. Other terms: Hx — history; Dx — diagnosis; Rx — treatment/prescription; NPO/NBM — nothing by mouth.
keyPoints: bd = twice daily; tds = three times; qds = four times

material.heading: Normal adult vital signs
material.body: Temperature: 36.5–37.5 °C (fever ≥ 38 °C). Pulse: 60–100 beats per minute. Respiratory rate: 12–20 breaths per minute. Blood pressure: below 120/80 mmHg is optimal; hypertension is ≥ 140/90 mmHg on repeated readings. Oxygen saturation (SpO2): 95–100% on room air. Pain is increasingly recorded as the 'fifth vital sign'.

questions.stem: 'tds' on a prescription means:
questions.explanation: tds = ter die sumendum, three times a day.

questions.stem: 'prn' means:
questions.explanation: prn = pro re nata, as required.

questions.stem: A normal adult respiratory rate is:
questions.explanation: Adults normally breathe 12–20 times per minute.

questions.stem: Which blood pressure reading, if sustained, indicates hypertension?
questions.explanation: Hypertension is ≥ 140/90 mmHg on repeated measurement.

questions.stem: 'stat' means:
questions.explanation: stat (statim) = at once.

questions.stem: The route 'SC' refers to:
questions.explanation: SC = subcutaneous injection.

questions.stem: A normal resting adult pulse is:
questions.explanation: Normal adult resting heart rate is 60–100 bpm.

questions.stem: A patient kept 'NBM' before surgery should:
questions.explanation: NBM/NPO = nil by mouth.
